original_question: For every inaccessible cardinal κ that is not weakly compact, must the negative relation \((2^κ over κ) ↛ (2^κ over κ)^(1,1)_2\) hold?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 4.2: whether \binom{2^\kappa}{\kappa} \nrightarrow \binom{2^\kappa}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2 holds for every inaccessible but not weakly compact cardinal \kappa. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's exact target almost verbatim: it asks about every inaccessible but not weakly compact cardinal \kappa, it uses the correct left-hand size 2^\kappa rather than \kappa^+, and it asks for the negative strong polarized relation rather than a consistency statement. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
missing_details: The draft does not unpack the paper's ambient notation. By Definition 1.1, the positive relation \binom{\lambda}{\kappa} \rightarrow \binom{\lambda}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2 means that for every coloring c: \lambda × \kappa → 2 there are A ⊆ \lambda and B ⊆ \kappa with |A| = \lambda and |B| = \kappa such that c is constant on A × B. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, the negative arrow should be spelled out as the failure of that property: there exists a 2-coloring c: 2^\kappa × \kappa → 2 for which no A ⊆ 2^\kappa and B ⊆ \kappa with |A| = 2^\kappa and |B| = \kappa make c constant on A × B. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))

The draft leaves implicit that this is a direct universal question about all such cardinals, as posed in Problem 4.2, not a forcing/consistency question like the adjacent Problems 4.3 and 4.4. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))

The paper treats this as a question about the strong polarized relation at uncountable cardinals, motivated by the nearby positive supercompact case; adding that context helps make the scope and intent explicit. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
refined_question: For every inaccessible but not weakly compact cardinal \kappa, does the negative strong polarized partition relation \binom{2^\kappa}{\kappa} \nrightarrow \binom{2^\kappa}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2 hold; that is, is there a coloring c: 2^\kappa × \kappa → 2 such that for no sets A ⊆ 2^\kappa and B ⊆ \kappa with |A| = 2^\kappa and |B| = \kappa is c constant on A × B? ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 4 rather than the singular-cardinal material around Proposition 1.2: the exact paper match is Problem 4.2, which asks this question for inaccessible non-weakly-compact cardinals and with the pair (2^\kappa, \kappa). Definition 1.1 supplies the meaning of the polarized notation, and the surrounding discussion in Section 4 frames Problem 4.2 as the 'small large cardinal' analogue of the supercompact positive result recalled from Theorem 2.3. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
